title: Why Britain Just Ended 14 Years of Conservative Rule

sentences.zh: 在太空的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您理解世界，充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅即可享受特别优惠，网址为 nytimes.com 加上斜杠 subscribe。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特罗夫，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: For more than a decade, Britain has been governed by conservatives who push the UK to the right, embracing smaller government and Brexit.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，英国一直由保守党统治，他们将英国推向右翼，拥护小政府和脱欧。

sentences.en: Last week, that era officially came to an end.
sentences.zh: 上周，那个时代正式结束了。

sentences.en: My colleague Mark Landler explains why UK voters rejected the Conservative Party and what a win by the British left means in a world where right-wing populism is on the rise.
sentences.zh: 我的同事马克·兰德尔解释了为什么英国选民拒绝保守党，以及在右翼民粹主义兴起的今天，英国左翼的胜利意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, July 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月10日，星期三。

sentences.en: Mark, hi.
sentences.zh: 马克，你好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Hi there, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 你好，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: I want to start this conversation by just asking you to help us break down what exactly happened in the UK elections last week.
sentences.zh: 我想从请你帮我们剖析上周英国大选究竟发生了什么开始今天的对话。

sentences.en: Well, the top line was the Conservative Party, which has been in government here for 14 years, was swept out in a resounding landslide by the Labour Party.
sentences.zh: 好的，最主要的情况是，已经执政14年的保守党在工党的压倒性胜利中被横扫出局。

sentences.en: So remember, the Conservatives, often known as the Tories, are the right-of-center party.
sentences.zh: 记住，保守党通常被称为托利党，是中右翼政党。

sentences.en: Labour is traditionally the left-of-center party, closely allied with the trade unions.
sentences.zh: 工党传统上是中左翼政党，与工会联系紧密。

sentences.en: So what happened in this election is that Labour won more than 400 seats in the Parliament compared to only 121 seats for the Conservatives.
sentences.zh: 所以这次选举中发生的事情是，工党在议会中赢得了400多个席位，而保守党只有121个席位。

sentences.en: And so that puts the Labour leader, Keir Starmer, into 10 Downing Street as the Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 这使得工党领袖基尔·斯塔默入主唐宁街10号成为首相。

sentences.en: It opens a new chapter in British politics after more than a decade of Conservative rule,
sentences.zh: 它开启了英国政治在经历十多年保守党统治后的新篇章，

sentences.en: and it represents a resounding repudiation of the Conservatives by a very angry electorate.
sentences.zh: 这也代表了一个愤怒的选民群体对保守党的彻底唾弃。

sentences.en: This is just a massive shift.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: What caused that turnaround after a decade-plus of Conservative rule?
sentences.zh: 十多年保守党统治之后，是什么导致了这种逆转？

sentences.en: What made the British voters reject the Tories in this election?
sentences.zh: 是什么让英国选民在这次选举中抛弃了托利党？

sentences.en: There were really three underlying issues that accumulated in a way that simply turned voters against them.
sentences.zh: 实际上有三个潜在问题累积起来，最终导致选民背叛了他们。

sentences.en: So I'd start with the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以我先从经济谈起。

sentences.en: It's the bedrock issue, the one that really underlies everything else.
sentences.zh: 这是最根本的问题，真正决定其他一切的问题。

sentences.en: And that story starts back in 2010, when the Conservatives first come back into government.
sentences.zh: 这个故事要追溯到2010年，当时保守党刚重新执政。

sentences.en: Our economy is stuck in a rut, and we need change to get it moving.
sentences.zh: 我们的经济陷入了困境，我们需要变革来推动它前进。

sentences.en: Let me tell you what I would do.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你我会怎么做。

sentences.en: At that time, they positioned themselves as the responsible stewards coming in in the aftermath of the global financial crisis to get Britain's house back in order,
sentences.zh: 当时，他们把自己定位为负责任的管理者，在全球金融危机之后上台，来整理英国的烂摊子，

sentences.en: to put Britain back on a responsible course.
sentences.zh: 让英国重回负责任的正轨。

sentences.en: Britain's budget deficit is so huge, says David Cameron, that cuts of a massive £83 billion are needed.
sentences.zh: 大卫·卡梅伦表示，英国的预算赤字如此巨大，以至于需要进行高达830亿英镑的巨额削减。

sentences.en: It'll be the most dramatic cutback of government spending since the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 这将是自20世纪20年代以来最戏剧性的政府开支削减。

sentences.en: And so they embarked on this period that's known as fiscal austerity.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始了被称为财政紧缩的时期。

sentences.en: They basically cut back funding for everything.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上削减了所有方面的资金。

sentences.en: They include 500,000 layoffs, cuts in welfare benefits, and major cuts in the military.
sentences.zh: 其中包括裁员50万人、削减福利补贴以及对军队的大幅削减。

sentences.en: In a sense, it balanced the books.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这平衡了账目。

sentences.en: But it did so at a great cost to the economy and to public life in Britain.
sentences.zh: 但代价是巨大的，损害了英国的经济和公共生活。

sentences.en: The report by the International Monetary Fund did warn that austerity measures may be jeopardizing growth.
sentences.zh: 国际货币基金组织的报告确实警告称，紧缩措施可能会危及经济增长。

sentences.en: Britain ended up with a very slow-growth economy, slow growth in wages that left people feeling that they weren't growing any more prosperous, that they weren't growing wealthier,
sentences.zh: 英国最终迎来了增长非常缓慢的经济，工资增长缓慢，让人们觉得他们不再变得更加繁荣，不再变得更加富有，

sentences.en: and sort of built up this accumulated sense that things were on the wrong track.
sentences.zh: 并逐渐积聚起一种“事情正走上歧路”的感觉。

sentences.en: And then there is this tumultuous event.
sentences.zh: 接下来是这个动荡的事件。

sentences.en: Brexit.
sentences.zh: 脱欧。

sentences.en: Brexit.
sentences.zh: 脱欧。

sentences.en: Brexit.
sentences.zh: 脱欧。

sentences.en: Brexit.
sentences.zh: 脱欧。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is Brexit.
sentences.zh: 当然，那就是脱欧。

sentences.en: I will go to Parliament and propose that the British people decide our future in Europe.
sentences.zh: 我将去议会提议，由英国人民决定我们在欧洲的未来。

sentences.en: Recall in 2016, the Conservative Prime Minister, David Cameron, called a referendum in which British voters were asked, do you want to remain in the European Union or leave?
sentences.zh: 回想2016年，保守党首相大卫·卡梅伦举行了一场全民公投，询问英国选民：你们想留在欧盟还是离开？

sentences.en: And there is this shock result.
sentences.zh: 结果令人震惊。

sentences.en: The British people have spoken, and the answer is, we're out.
sentences.zh: 英国人民已经发声，答案是：我们退出。

sentences.en: That Britain votes to leave the EU.
sentences.zh: 英国投票决定离开欧盟。

sentences.en: Is the UK economy standing at the cliff edge?
sentences.zh: 英国经济正站在悬崖边上吗？

sentences.en: Or is there a soft landing the other side of Brexit?
sentences.zh: 还是脱欧之后会有软着陆？

sentences.en: And that adds yet another layer of drag on the economy.
sentences.zh: 这给经济带来了又一层拖累。

sentences.en: The EU was and is Britain's largest trading partner.
sentences.zh: 欧盟过去是、现在仍然是英国最大的贸易伙伴。

sentences.en: Cutting those ties meant that suddenly trade became much more difficult, bureaucracy much more cumbersome,
sentences.zh: 切断这些联系意味着贸易突然变得更加困难，官僚作风更加繁琐，

sentences.en: and a general sense among businesses both within the UK and outside the UK that maybe Britain wasn't as good a place to inveSt.
sentences.zh: 英国国内外的企业普遍认为英国可能不再是一个好的投资场所。

sentences.en: So there's almost a sense of this as a lost decade.
sentences.zh: 因此，这几乎带有一种“失去的十年”的感觉。

sentences.en: People feel that the British economy has been treading water, and their own personal situations have not gotten any better.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得英国经济一直在原地踏步，他们自己的个人处境也没有变得更好。

sentences.en: So at the end of this lost decade, do voters start to question whether the Tories are, in fact, the responsible economic stewards they had said they were?
sentences.zh: 那么在这失去的十年结束时，选民开始质疑托利党是否真的是他们自称的负责任的经济管理者吗？

sentences.en: Well, you might think this would be the moment that they would turn on the Tories.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为这会是他们抛弃托利党的时刻。

sentences.en: But in fact, the Tories managed to get themselves another term in the 2019 election.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，托利党在2019年的大选中设法又赢得了一个任期。

sentences.en: And they stumbled on through a couple more prime ministers.
sentences.zh: 他们磕磕绊绊地熬过了又几位首相。

sentences.en: The economic crisis didn't really turn into a political disaster for the Tories until Liz Truss.
sentences.zh: 直到莉兹·特拉斯上台，经济危机才真正演变成托利党的政治灾难。

sentences.en: Remind us who Liz Truss is.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下我们莉兹·特拉斯是谁。

sentences.en: So Liz Truss is the prime minister who came in right after Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 莉兹·特拉斯是紧随鲍里斯·约翰逊之后的首相。

sentences.en: And what Liz Truss did is she came in and she basically tried an ideological experiment on the British economy.
sentences.zh: 莉兹·特拉斯所做的是，她上台后基本上在英国经济上进行了一场意识形态实验。

sentences.en: She tried to pass very radical, very sweeping, and completely unfunded tax cuts.
sentences.zh: 她试图通过非常激进、非常全面且完全没有资金支持的减税政策。

sentences.en: And it had the effect of spooking the financial markets, sending the British pound into a tailspin,
sentences.zh: 这吓坏了金融市场，导致英镑暴跌，

sentences.en: and basically wrecking the confidence of both the domestic audience as well as international investors in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 并基本上摧毁了国内观众以及国际投资者对英国的信心。

sentences.en: And in a matter of weeks, Liz Truss managed to undo whatever reputation the conservative party had built over decades for responsibly managing the economy.
sentences.zh: 在短短几周内，莉兹·特拉斯就毁掉了保守党数十年来建立的负责任管理经济的声誉。

sentences.en: And she resigns on her 44th day in office.
sentences.zh: 她在上任第44天辞职。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: This incredibly brief tenure of Liz Truss was really the straw that broke the camel's back here after more than a decade of economic trouble.
sentences.zh: 经历了十多年的经济困境后，莉兹·特拉斯极其短暂的任期真的是压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The British voters were frustrated, to be sure, and discontent.
sentences.zh: 英国选民当然感到沮丧和不满。

sentences.en: But not until Truss came along did the party really forfeit its reputation for knowing how to manage the economy.
sentences.zh: 但直到特拉斯出现，该党才真正失去了其懂经济管理的声誉。

sentences.en: After Truss, I think a majority of voters in this country simply decided we can't, if you will, trust these people with our economy.
sentences.zh: 在特拉斯之后，我认为这个国家的大多数选民干脆决定，恕我直言，我们不能把经济交托给这些人。

sentences.en: And what do things look like now?
sentences.zh: 现在情况怎么样了？

sentences.en: Well, one of the things that's very striking about the U.K.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于今天的英国，非常引人注目的一点是，

sentences.en: today is you have this very dynamic, vibrant capital city, London, which accounts for a disproportionate amount of economic activity in the country.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一个非常充满活力、生机勃勃的首都伦敦，它占据了这个国家不成比例的经济活动量。

sentences.en: And then you've got the hinterland, which in the U.K.
sentences.zh: 然后是腹地，在英国，

sentences.en: can be a fairly depressing place.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个相当令人沮丧的地方。

sentences.en: The Midlands, the North, this is the old industrial belt.
sentences.zh: 米德兰兹，北方，这是老工业地带。

sentences.en: It would be the equivalent of the Rust Belt in the American MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 这相当于美国中西部的铁锈地带。

sentences.en: And these are places that have really suffered during this long period of austerity.
sentences.zh: 这些地方在漫长的紧缩时期真的遭受了苦难。

sentences.en: So if you go into some of these towns, you see boarded up storefronts, you see shuttered factories,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你走进其中一些城镇，你会看到用木板封住的店面，看到关闭的工厂，

sentences.en: you see a lot of people on public assistance, a lot of people who are not physically all that well.
sentences.zh: 你会看到很多靠公共援助的人，许多身体状况不太好的人。

sentences.en: And it is true, and it's a statistic that's often mentioned in this country, that if you take London out of the equation on a GDP per capita basis,
sentences.zh: 确实如此，这也是这个国家经常被提及的一个统计数据，如果你把伦敦从人均GDP的方程式中剔除，

sentences.en: which is a very common way of measuring wealth, the rest of England is roughly equivalent to the state of Mississippi, which is, of course, one of the poorest states in America.
sentences.zh: 这是衡量财富的一种非常常见的方法，英国其他地区大致相当于美国最贫穷的州之一密西西比州。

sentences.en: So that's one way of thinking about the Britain of 2024.
sentences.zh: 所以这是思考2024年英国的一种方式。

sentences.en: It's a major contrast between London and the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 伦敦与国家其他地区之间存在巨大的对比。

sentences.en: So it sounds like the economy is really struggling, and people are starting to lay blame at the feet of the Tories.
sentences.zh: 听起来经济确实在苦苦挣扎，人们开始将责任归咎于托利党。

sentences.en: So that's one explanation for why the public turns on this party.
sentences.zh: 所以这是公众抛弃这个政党的一个解释。

sentences.en: What else is at play?
sentences.zh: 还有什么在起作用？

sentences.en: Well, there's a second issue, and it's not unconnected from the first issue, and that is the state of the National Health Service.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有第二个问题，它与第一个问题并非毫无关系，那就是国民医疗服务体系（NHS）的现状。

sentences.en: Across the UK, hospitals are at breaking point.
sentences.zh: 在整个英国，医院正处于崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: The beloved national public hospital network that tens of millions of Brits rely on every single day.
sentences.zh: 这是数千万英国人每天都依赖的深受喜爱的国家公共医院网络。

sentences.en: They are running out of beds, and the patients keep coming.
sentences.zh: 他们的床位快用完了，而病人源源不断。

sentences.en: This also has been a victim of years and years of austerity, of cost-cutting, or of very small budget increases.
sentences.zh: 这也是多年来紧缩政策、削减成本或极少预算增长的受害者。

sentences.en: The waiting room was rammed.
sentences.zh: 候诊室挤得水泄不通。

sentences.en: Trollies were just piling up in the hallway.
sentences.zh: 担架在走廊里堆成了山。

sentences.en: What you see are incredible lines in emergency rooms at big public hospitals.
sentences.zh: 你看到的是大型公立医院急诊室里排起的惊人长队。

sentences.en: Seven and a half million people in England now on a waiting list for hospital treatment.
sentences.zh: 英格兰现在有七百五十万人排队等待医院治疗。

sentences.en: If you make an appointment for elective surgery, you're often put on a waiting list for 8 months, 10 months, 12, or even 14 months.
sentences.zh: 如果你预约了选择性手术，你通常会被列入8个月、10个月、12个月甚至14个月的等待名单。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Even if you're a cancer patient, you might not get immediate treatment because the system is simply so overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 即使你是癌症患者，你也可能无法立即得到治疗，因为这个系统简直是不堪重负。

sentences.en: Staff shortages are now leading to fears for patient safety.
sentences.zh: 人员短缺现在导致人们对患者安全感到担忧。

sentences.en: And after years and years of chronic underinvestment...
sentences.zh: 在经历了一年又一年的长期投资不足之后……

sentences.en: One junior doctor said she was quitting after just one year.
sentences.zh: 一名初级医生说她在仅仅工作一年后就辞职了。

sentences.en: Paul Pei cited as the first reason for such a drastic move.
sentences.zh: 保罗·培伊被列为做出如此激进举动的第一原因。

sentences.en: It simply doesn't have the physical resources, the human capital resources, the doctors, the nurses.
sentences.zh: 它根本没有物质资源、人力资本资源、医生、护士。

sentences.en: And so you just have this sense of a country that feels a bit hollowed out.
sentences.zh: 所以你就会有一种这个国家被掏空的感觉。

sentences.en: We haven't got enough doctors.
sentences.zh: 我们没有足够的医生。

sentences.en: The governments aren't funding the NHS properly.
sentences.zh: 政府没有对NHS进行适当的资助。

sentences.en: And this really has to stop.
sentences.zh: 这真的必须停止了。

sentences.en: This isn't, by the way, just true in the health care area, but it's most palpable and really most visible to citizens in the NHS.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这不仅适用于医疗保健领域，而且对NHS的公民来说是最切实、最明显的。

sentences.en: Part of the Tories' identity, right, is that they were the party of fiscal responsibility, that they were the best stewards of the economy.
sentences.zh: 保守党身份的一部分，对吧，就是他们是财政责任党，他们是最好的经济管理者。

sentences.en: And it sounds like that really is no longer holding up in Britain and that they've actually become seen as the ones who are causing these very real problems, everyday problems,
sentences.zh: 听起来这在英国已经不再站得住脚了，他们实际上被视为造成这些非常真实的问题、日常问题的人，

sentences.en: for the average voter.
sentences.zh: 对于普通选民而言。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: I think that to the average voter, the mismanagement of the economy became linked to other things that affected the quality of their everyday lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为对普通选民来说，经济管理不善与其他影响他们日常生活质量的事情联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And then there's a final thing, and also very core to the identity of the modern conservative party.
sentences.zh: 然后还有最后一件事，这也是现代保守党身份的核心。

sentences.en: One of the major arguments that the pro-Brexit people made was that this will enable us to cut down on mass, uncontrolled immigration.
sentences.zh: 亲脱欧人士提出的主要论点之一是，这将使我们能够减少大规模的、不受控制的移民。

sentences.en: And they failed utterly in that goal as well.
sentences.zh: 他们在那个目标上也彻底失败了。

sentences.en: The number of net arrivals in the country has gone up from 300,000 to 780,000.
sentences.zh: 该国的净入境人数已从30万上升到78万。

sentences.en: So rather than declining after Brexit, immigration soared.
sentences.zh: 因此，移民非但没有在脱欧后下降，反而激增了。

sentences.en: How did that happen?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: Why didn't immigration go down after Brexit if that was the big promise?
sentences.zh: 如果那是最大的承诺，为什么脱欧后移民没有减少？

sentences.en: Well, this is one of the interesting paradoxes of the whole Brexit period.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是整个脱欧时期有趣的悖论之一。

sentences.en: This is the first time in nearly 40 years where the British government will be in control and will determine its own immigration policy.
sentences.zh: 这是近40年来英国政府第一次掌权并决定自己的移民政策。

sentences.en: When Britain left the European Union, it did actually end freedom of travel for people from the European Union.
sentences.zh: 当英国离开欧盟时，它确实结束了欧盟人民的自由旅行权。

sentences.en: We are bringing an end to a free movement of labour, which of course is linked to our membership of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 我们正在结束劳动力自由流动，这当然与我们成为欧盟成员国有关。

sentences.en: So what you saw much less of in London, for example, was waiters from Italy, Greece, Spain, in restaurants.
sentences.zh: 所以你在伦敦看到的情况是，例如餐馆里来自意大利、希腊、西班牙的服务员少了很多。

sentences.en: But what the government was doing, you know, rather quietly, was changing the immigration rules.
sentences.zh: 但政府正在做的，你知道，悄悄地在做，是改变移民规则。

sentences.en: Some important news today on long-term migration into the UK.
sentences.zh: 今天关于长期移居英国有一些重要新闻。

sentences.en: In the 8th of June, there's been a surge in long-term immigration.
sentences.zh: 在6月8日，长期移民出现了激增。

sentences.en: So that rather than allowing relatively young, unskilled workers from the EU, the country began being more open to much higher-skilled people from other parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 因此，该国没有允许来自欧盟的相对年轻、非熟练的工人，而是开始对来自世界其他地区的高技能人员更加开放。

sentences.en: Now, the jump is caused by a rise in non-EU migration with special factors at play.
sentences.zh: 现在，这一跃升是由非欧盟移民的增加以及特殊因素的作用引起的。

sentences.en: Overseas students coming back to the UK as COVID restrictions have relapsed.
sentences.zh: 随着新冠疫情限制措施的解除，留学生们正重新回到英国。

sentences.en: So while you see much fewer Polish plumbers, for example, you see many more Indian, Sri Lankan, Pakistani doctors.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然比如波兰水管工明显变少了，但印度、斯里兰卡和巴基斯坦的医生却多了很多。

sentences.en: Special support to people from Ukraine and Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 对来自乌克兰和香港的人士提供特别支持。

sentences.en: And of course...
sentences.zh: 当然还有……

sentences.en: You see many more Filipina nurses.
sentences.zh: 菲律宾籍护士也多了很多。

sentences.en: And of course, the impact of the Afghan resettlement program.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有阿富汗人安置计划的影响。

sentences.en: Many more graduate students from Nigeria or other parts of Africa.
sentences.zh: 来自尼日利亚或非洲其他地区的研究生也更多了。

sentences.en: So immigration didn't decline.
sentences.zh: 所以移民并没有减少。

sentences.en: It's the nature of immigration changed.
sentences.zh: 而是移民的性质变了。

sentences.en: Does that make people mad?
sentences.zh: 这会惹恼大家吗？

sentences.en: Because I think we're used to seeing in the U.S., at least,
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得我们至少在美国已经习惯了看到这样的现象：

sentences.en: that the frustration and resentment towards immigrants is usually related to the people who are coming in and are in more desperate situations.
sentences.zh: 对移民的沮丧和怨恨通常与那些涌入且处于更绝望境地的人有关。

sentences.en: Not folks getting angry about doctors or lawyers from abroad.
sentences.zh: 而不是对来自国外的医生或律师感到愤怒的人。

sentences.en: It's a very complicated issue.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常复杂的问题。

sentences.en: And I'm glad you asked it this way.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你以这种方式提问。

sentences.en: Because it is in fact true that for many English people, going to a hospital and being treated by an Indian doctor does not arouse any resentment.
sentences.zh: 因为事实确实如此，对许多英国人来说，去医院看病并由印度医生治疗并不会引起任何怨恨。

sentences.en: They're grateful that they have a doctor who's able to see them.
sentences.zh: 他们很感激能有医生为他们看病。

sentences.en: The problem arises more from immigration in the aggregate.
sentences.zh: 问题更多地源于整体上的移民。

sentences.en: The net migration to this country has increased massively.
sentences.zh: 这个国家的净移民人数大幅增加。

sentences.en: There's this sense that the borders have been thrown open.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种国门大开的感觉。

sentences.en: How many more houses do we have to build?
sentences.zh: 我们还得建造多少房子？

sentences.en: That immigration is out of control.
sentences.zh: 大家觉得移民失控了。

sentences.en: Are they being schooled and educated and looked after by our social and health services?
sentences.zh: 我们的社会和医疗服务能够为他们提供学校教育和照顾吗？

sentences.en: That's my main concern.
sentences.zh: 这是我最主要担心的。

sentences.en: How are we going to be able to cope?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何应对？

sentences.en: Because we're not really coping now, are we?
sentences.zh: 因为我们现在其实应付不过来，对吧？

sentences.en: So there is this kind of nagging sense on the part of many people, by the way, it's not just people on the right, that immigration has gotten out of control,
sentences.zh: 所以许多人有一种挥之不去的感觉——顺便说一句，不仅是右翼人士——那就是移民已经失控了，

sentences.en: that this government had promised to sort of bring it under control.
sentences.zh: 而现政府曾承诺将其控制住。

sentences.en: And instead, the opposite seems to be happening.
sentences.zh: 但相反的情况似乎正在发生。

sentences.en: Basically, it sounds like there's a lot of people who wanted Brexit specifically to reduce migration.
sentences.zh: 基本上，听起来有很多人希望通过英国脱欧来专门减少移民。

sentences.en: These are folks who felt betrayed by the Tories because they got the opposite result.
sentences.zh: 这些人对保守党感到背叛，因为他们得到了相反的结果。

sentences.en: And that's part of a bigger thread here, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是更大主线的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: This is a story about mismanagement of core issues for the British public.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于英国公众核心问题管理不善的故事。

sentences.en: The economy's a mess, immigration's rising, the health care system is rife with dysfunction.
sentences.zh: 经济一团糟，移民不断上升，医疗系统弊病丛生。

sentences.en: So is it fair to see the results of the election as essentially a rejection of conservatism in the UK and of the ideals that brought us Brexit,
sentences.zh: 那么，将这次选举结果基本上视为对英国保守主义以及带来英国脱欧的理想的拒绝，这公平吗？

sentences.en: which was so core to much of this story?
sentences.zh: 而这正是许多这类故事的核心？

sentences.en: I think it's certainly fair to see this election as a rejection of a party that failed at its most basic task, which was governing effectively and responsibly.
sentences.zh: 我认为，把这次选举看作是对一个未能完成最基本任务——即有效和负责任执政——的政党的拒绝，当然是公平的。

sentences.en: On the face of it, it looks like a triumph of the left.
sentences.zh: 表面上看，这像是左翼的胜利。

sentences.en: But when you dig into it, when you see how the voters voted, which parties did well, which did less well,
sentences.zh: 但当你深入探究，当你看到选民是如何投票的，哪些政党表现好，哪些表现不那么好时，

sentences.en: you get a much more complicated picture about what it is that voters really wanted.
sentences.zh: 你就会对选民真正想要什么有一个复杂得多的认识。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温纳露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《连连看》(Connections)这款游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是山姆·马祖斯基，我每天都创作《拼字蜜蜂》(Spelling Bee)和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“彩色联觉”(promesthesia)的病症。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由刚才你们听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 从今天开始游玩。

sentences.en: I wonder if you can explain why what looked like this huge win for the Labour Party is actually more complex.
sentences.zh: 我想请教您解释一下，为什么这场看似工党巨大胜利的背后其实要复杂得多？

sentences.en: I mean, on the face of it, it would seem to be the sweeping endorsement of the left.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，表面上看，这似乎是对左翼的压倒性支持。

sentences.en: Is that not what this is?
sentences.zh: 难道事实并非如此吗？

sentences.en: Well, you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得对。

sentences.en: On the face of it, it looks like a huge embrace of left-of-center politics.
sentences.zh: 表面上看，这似乎是对中左翼政治的巨大拥抱。

sentences.en: And in fact, the Labour Party performed very well in this election.
sentences.zh: 事实上，工党在这次选举中表现得非常好。

sentences.en: But the key thing to understand is, this is not the same Labour Party that ran in the last election in 2019.
sentences.zh: 但需要理解的关键一点是，这已经不是2019年参加上一届大选的那个工党了。

sentences.en: This Labour Party is far more centriSt.
sentences.zh: 这个工党要温和得多、更倾向于中间派。

sentences.en: And that's the result of a very methodical, deliberate plan on the part of the party's leader,
sentences.zh: 这是该党领袖基尔·斯塔默——他现在是首相——有计划、深思熟虑的政策结果，

sentences.en: Keir Starmer, who's now the prime minister, to pull the party away from some of its more leftist positions in an attempt to make it more acceptable to a broader range of voters.
sentences.zh: 他将该党从一些更左翼的立场上拉开，企图使其更能被更广泛的选民所接受。

sentences.en: How drastic of a turn to the centre are we talking about here, Mark?
sentences.zh: 马克，我们在这里讨论的是向中间派的大幅度转变吗？

sentences.en: It was a fairly radical move on the part of Starmer.
sentences.zh: 对斯塔默来说，这是一次相当激进的举动。

sentences.en: If you look at the old Labour Party, the party that ran in the 2019 election, this was a party that talked about re-nationalising the entire British electricity grid.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看老工党，也就是参加2019年大选的那个党，当时他们谈论的是将整个英国电网重新收归国有。

sentences.en: This was a party whose leader, Jeremy Corbyn, was openly sceptical about the role of NATO.
sentences.zh: 这个党的领袖杰里米·科尔宾对北约的作用公开持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: And in each of these areas, Starmer moved very deliberately.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些领域，斯塔默都采取了非常慎重的行动。

sentences.en: He pulled the national security policy much more to the centre, made the party feel much more patriotic.
sentences.zh: 他将国家安全政策向中间靠拢，让这个党显得更具爱国色彩。

sentences.en: He promised not to raise taxes on working people.
sentences.zh: 他承诺不增加劳动人民的税收。

sentences.en: He promised not to vastly expand spending until the country could afford it.
sentences.zh: 他承诺在国家负担得起之前，不会大幅扩大开支。

sentences.en: So across every one of these areas, it's more than just rebranding the party.
sentences.zh: 所以在每一个领域，这不仅仅是给政党重新包装。

sentences.en: Starmer really repositioned it and turned it into a centre-left party rather than a pure left-wing party.
sentences.zh: 斯塔默真正重新定位了该党，将其变成了一个中左翼政党，而不是纯粹的左翼政党。

sentences.en: Starmer, it sounds like, basically turns Labour into an alternative that wasn't all that different from the Tories.
sentences.zh: 听起来，斯塔默基本上把工党变成了一个与保守党没有太大区别的替代选择。

sentences.en: It just had much less baggage.
sentences.zh: 只是受到的历史包袱要少得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: It's an exaggeration to say that Labour is Tory 2.0.
sentences.zh: 说工党是“保守党2.0”未免有些夸张。

sentences.en: There are policy differences, but the fundamental pitch here is, if you elect us, we will do a better job than the Tories, but we won't give you a radically different government.
sentences.zh: 政策上确实存在差异，但其核心主张是：如果你们选我们，我们会比保守党做得更好，但我们不会给你们一个激进不同的政府。

sentences.en: And now, is that what's happened?
sentences.zh: 那么现在，情况确实如此吗？

sentences.en: I mean, is the Labour Party now the new standard-bearer in British politics, this broadly acceptable centrist party that most people can get behind?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，工党现在成了英国政治的新旗手、大多数人都能支持的广泛接受的中间派政党吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's no question that in terms of seats, they are going to be the political standard-bearer.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，从席位来看，他们将成为政治旗手。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing when you look to the actual raw vote is that the Labour Party didn't roll up the kind of crushing landslide
sentences.zh: 但当你查看实际的得票总数时，有趣的是，工党并没有赢得压倒性的巨大胜利，

sentences.en: that you would expect given how many seats they gained.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他们获得的席位，你本以为会有这样的结果。

sentences.en: Labour only got roughly a third of the raw vote, which is actually less than they got in 2017 when they lost to the Conservatives.
sentences.zh: 工党只获得了大约三分之一的原始选票，这实际上比他们在2017年输给保守党时还要少。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And that speaks to the fragmentation of the electorate.
sentences.zh: 这也说明了选民的分裂。

sentences.en: You had in this election not two parties, but four parties that performed well.
sentences.zh: 在这次选举中，表现出色的不是两个党，而是四个党。

sentences.en: In addition to Labour and the Conservatives, you had the Liberal Democrats, another centrist anti-Brexit party that did remarkably well.
sentences.zh: 除了工党和保守党，还有自由民主党，这是另一个表现非常出色的中间派反脱欧政党。

sentences.en: And then perhaps most interestingly, you had this new anti-immigration insurgent populist party,
sentences.zh: 然后，也许最有趣的是，出现了一个新的反移民民粹主义新兴政党：

sentences.en: Reform UK, that came out of nowhere and became a major factor.
sentences.zh: 英国改革党（Reform UK），它凭空出现并成为了一个主要因素。

sentences.en: Okay, what's the backstory of that party?
sentences.zh: 好的，这个党有什么背景故事？

sentences.en: So reform grows out of the Brexit debate.
sentences.zh: 改革党是从脱欧辩论中发展而来的。

sentences.en: And basically, this is a party that's almost a single-issue party.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是一个几乎只关注单一议题的政党。

sentences.en: It's an anti-immigration party.
sentences.zh: 这是一个反移民政党。

sentences.en: They basically argue that Britain needs to get this flood of immigrants under control.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上认为英国需要控制这股移民潮。

sentences.en: It's led by this very well-known, gleeful, insurgent politician named Nigel Farage.
sentences.zh: 它的领导人是一位非常知名、得意洋洋的政坛黑马尼格尔·法拉奇。

sentences.en: He's been a fixture on the right in Britain for more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，他一直是英国右翼的常客。

sentences.en: He was one of the primary campaigners for Brexit.
sentences.zh: 他是英国脱欧的主要活动家之一。

sentences.en: And he fielded hundreds and hundreds of candidates in this election.
sentences.zh: 他在这次选举中派出了成百上千名候选人。

sentences.en: And what they wound up doing was siphoning off a lot of the Conservative vote.
sentences.zh: 他们最终做的事情是分流了大量的保守党选票。

sentences.en: And how typical is it to see this many parties do well in UK politics?
sentences.zh: 在英国政治中，看到这么多政党表现出色有多常见？

sentences.en: I mean, what do you make of the fact that these smaller, more obscure groups were able to do so well?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些较小、更晦涩的群体能够表现得如此出色，你怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, it is quite unusual.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很不寻常。

sentences.en: And it speaks to a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 这说明了几个问题。

sentences.en: One is that you have an electorate that, particularly among young voters, is much less loyal to the major parties.
sentences.zh: 一是你拥有一群选民，特别是年轻选民，对主要政党的忠诚度要低得多。

sentences.en: So in this election, Labour and the Conservatives together got only 57% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 因此在这次选举中，工党和保守党加起来只获得了57%的选票。

sentences.en: That's the lowest combined percentage for the major parties at any time in the post-World War II period.
sentences.zh: 这是二战以来主要政党获得的总得票率的最低纪录。

sentences.en: So that's the overarching dynamic.
sentences.zh: 所以这是总体的动态。

sentences.en: But there's something very interesting going on with votes on the right.
sentences.zh: 但右翼选票中发生了一些非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: In this election, you had a number of Conservative voters vote for Reform UK as a way of registering their unhappiness with the Conservative Party,
sentences.zh: 在这次选举中，许多保守党选民投票给英国改革党，以此来表达他们对保守党的不满，

sentences.en: particularly on the issue of immigration.
sentences.zh: 特别是在移民问题上。

sentences.en: They knew that those votes would help ensure that a Labour Party got into government, but they were less worried by that prospect.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这些选票将有助于确保工党上台，但他们对这种前景不那么担心。

sentences.en: In the old days, with that old, much more left Labour Party,
sentences.zh: 过去，面对那个更左翼的旧工党，

sentences.en: Conservative voters would have been much more reluctant not to stick with their own party for fear of allowing the opposition to get into power.
sentences.zh: 保守党选民会更加不愿意背离自己的政党，生怕让反对派掌权。

sentences.en: This new Labour Party, this more centrist Labour Party, did not scare them the same way.
sentences.zh: 这个新工党，这个更温和的工党，并没有以同样的方式吓退他们。

sentences.en: And in a funny way, that empowered them and enabled them to cast that protest vote for Reform UK.
sentences.zh: 从某种滑稽的角度来看，这赋予了他们力量，使他们能够为英国改革党投下抗议票。

sentences.en: And that's really what split the vote on the right and allowed Labour to do so well.
sentences.zh: 这确实分裂了右翼的选票，并让工党取得了如此好的成绩。

sentences.en: So you have these Conservative voters who are still out there who want to punish the Tories, and now they feel like they can
sentences.zh: 所以你有一些保守党选民仍然想惩罚保守党，现在他们觉得他们可以这样做了，

sentences.en: because they're not as scared, right, about a Labour victory because Labour is just more palatable at this point.
sentences.zh: 因为他们对工党获胜不再那么害怕，对吧，因为工党现在更容易让人接受了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Labour has not threatened to raise their taxes.
sentences.zh: 工党没有威胁要加税。

sentences.en: It hasn't threatened to blow out the budget.
sentences.zh: 它没有威胁要搞垮预算。

sentences.en: It hasn't threatened to do all the things a Labour government might have done five years ago.
sentences.zh: 它没有威胁要做五年前工党政府可能会做的那些事情。

sentences.en: And as a result, voting for Nigel Farage and his party seems like a less risky thing to do.
sentences.zh: 因此，投票给尼格尔·法拉奇和他的政党似乎是一件风险较小的事情。

sentences.en: So, Mark, this is a much more complicated picture for the Labour Party, which is now, you know, running the government.
sentences.zh: 所以，马克，对于现在掌权执政的工党来说，情况要复杂得多。

sentences.en: This is hardly a decisive win for them, an endorsement of their ideology.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是他们的决定性胜利，也不是对他们意识形态的认可。

sentences.en: How do you think they're seeing it?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们是怎么看待这个结果的？

sentences.en: Well, I think they recognize that because of all the issues we discussed, their relatively low raw vote total, the fragmentation of the voters,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他们认识到，由于我们讨论的所有问题，他们相对较低的得票总数，选民的分裂，

sentences.en: the fact that other parties have done so well, that they need to produce results quickly, that they're dealing with an impatient electorate, a volatile electorate, fickle voters
sentences.zh: 以及其他政党表现得如此出色，他们需要迅速取得成果，因为他们面对的是一个没有耐心的选民群体、一个反复无常的选民群体、变化无常的选民，

sentences.en: who are not going to cut them a lot of slack.
sentences.zh: 他们不会给工党太多的宽容空间。

sentences.en: They know that in less than five years, the Conservatives managed to turn a landslide victory into a landslide defeat.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，在不到五年的时间里，保守党就把一场压倒性的胜利变成了惨败。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they don't want to suffer the same fate.
sentences.zh: 他们不想遭遇同样的命运。

sentences.en: So Starmer, I think, is going to try that within a year or two, he can say to voters, look, you elected me to be more competent.
sentences.zh: 所以我想斯塔默会努力在一两年内对选民说：看，你们选我是为了让我更有能力。

sentences.en: You elected me to turn around this economy.
sentences.zh: 你们选我是为了让我扭转这个国家的经济。

sentences.en: This is what I've done.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所做的。

sentences.en: Judge me on that.
sentences.zh: 以此来评判我吧。

sentences.en: And then I think if he can pull that off, he has a very good shot of getting a second term.
sentences.zh: 然后我认为，如果他能做到这一点，他将很有希望赢得第二个任期。

sentences.en: Starmer wants to move fast here.
sentences.zh: 斯塔默在这里希望迅速采取行动。

sentences.en: But, I mean, it strikes me that all the issues we talked about, these challenges he's staring down, are pretty hard to turn around quickly.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，在我看来，我们讨论的所有这些问题，他所面临的这些挑战，要想迅速扭转局面是相当困难的。

sentences.en: I mean, fixing the economy in the midst of global economic uncertainty, fixing a starved healthcare system, immigration.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在全球经济不确定性的情况下修复经济，修复一个资源匮乏的医疗系统，还有移民问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, you raised exactly the right point.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，你点到了正题。

sentences.en: Starmer's in this very difficult situation where he needs to show some quick wins, but a lot of the remedies are long-term, and there's an added problem.
sentences.zh: 斯塔默处在一个非常艰难的境地，他需要展现一些快速的成果，但许多解决办法都是长期的，还有一个额外的问题。

sentences.en: He has no money.
sentences.zh: 他没有钱。

sentences.en: So he has to do all this with an empty larder, if you will, and that's going to be perhaps the biggest challenge of all.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须在一个空空如也的米缸里做这一切，如果你愿意这么说的话，这可能将是最大的挑战。

sentences.en: How do you show wins when you don't have many tools to work with?
sentences.zh: 当你没有什么工具可用时，你如何展现出成果？

sentences.en: Right, and waiting in the wings, you have these smaller groups, right, including this far-right anti-immigrant party that, you know, is looking to see what happens
sentences.zh: 没错，在场外虎视眈眈的还有这些小党派，对吧，包括这个极右翼的反移民政党，你知道的，它正拭目以待，

sentences.en: and prepared to capitalize on any weakness, I'd assume.
sentences.zh: 随时准备利用任何弱点，我猜。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Even though the reform party won only five seats in parliament, one of those seats belongs to Nigel Farage, and he is going to be taking shots at the labor government,
sentences.zh: 尽管改革党在议会中只赢得了五个席位，但其中一个席位属于尼格尔·法拉奇，他将向工党政府开炮，

sentences.en: pointing out every single shortcoming, with an eye to building up his party over time, so that if labor really fails in three, four, or five years,
sentences.zh: 指出每一个缺点，着眼于随着时间的推移壮大他的政党，这样如果工党在三、四、五年后真的失败了，

sentences.en: reform might not just be an insurgent party, it might actually be a party positioned to either play a kingmaker role or really be a dominant presence in British politics.
sentences.zh: 改革党可能不仅仅是一个新兴政党，它实际上可能成为一个有能力发挥造王者作用或在英国政坛占据主导地位的政党。

sentences.en: Mark, that leads me to ask you how you're thinking about the stakes here, and not just for the U.K., but for the world.
sentences.zh: 马克，这让我忍不住想问你，你是如何看待这里的利害关系的，不仅对英国，对全世界也是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, what would it mean for the Labor Party to fail?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，工党如果失败意味着什么？

sentences.en: I think failure would have a profound consequence for liberal democracies in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为失败将对西方自由民主制度产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, remember, France is currently dealing with a surging hard-right movement in its parliamentary elections.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，记住，法国目前在其议会选举中正在应对来势汹汹的极右翼运动。

sentences.en: The Germans dealt with hard-right advances in recent European elections.
sentences.zh: 德国在最近的欧洲议会选举中也应对了极右翼势力的推进。

sentences.en: And in a matter of months, voters in America may elect Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 而在几个月内，美国的选民可能会选出唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: So I think that the failure of the Labor Party would reinforce a populist wave that appears to be building in many of these countries.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，工党的失败将巩固这许多国家中似乎正在成型的民粹主义浪潮。

sentences.en: And success?
sentences.zh: 那如果成功呢？

sentences.en: If the Labor Party can show that a centrist government can function effectively in a world as buffeted by all of these populist, more extremist trends,
sentences.zh: 如果工党能够证明，在一个饱受所有这些民粹主义和更极端趋势冲击的世界里，一个中间派政府能够有效运转，

sentences.en: you could foresee a world in three years where Keir Starmer, a successful center-left prime minister, almost stands as a bulwark for the rules-based international order.
sentences.zh: 你可以预见，三年后基尔·斯塔默作为一位成功的中间偏左首相，几乎可以成为以规则为基础的国际秩序的中流砥柱。

sentences.en: And this would be particularly true if Donald Trump were elected in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果唐纳德·特朗普在美国当选，

sentences.en: in November.
sentences.zh: 情况尤其会如此。

sentences.en: You know, the interesting precedent for this is Angela Merkel, who was the chancellor of Germany when Trump was in his first term as president and was widely viewed
sentences.zh: 你知道，这方面一个有趣的先例是安格拉·默克尔，当特朗普首次担任美国总统时，她是德国总理，并被广泛视为

sentences.en: as almost the leader of the liberal democratic world.
sentences.zh: 几乎是自由民主世界的领袖。

sentences.en: That's a role I think that Keir Starmer could potentially inhabit depending on how events play out.
sentences.zh: 我认为基尔·斯塔默也有可能扮演这样一个角色，这取决于事态的发展。

sentences.en: There's a lot of caveats here in both the U.S.
sentences.zh: 无论在美国还是在英国，

sentences.en: and in Britain.
sentences.zh: 都有很多需要说明的前提条件。

sentences.en: But I do think that Starmer has this potential to play a very, very significant role at an uncertain time in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，斯塔默有潜力在西方不确定的时期扮演非常非常重要的角色。

sentences.en: Mark, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 马克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks, Natalie.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，娜塔莉。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: Are you confident that President Biden has what it takes to win in November and serve the next four years?
sentences.zh: 你是否确信拜登总统具备在11月胜选并再服务四年的能力？

sentences.en: As I've said before, I'm with Joe.
sentences.zh: 正如我以前说过的，我支持乔。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Top congressional Democrats are indicating they are unwilling, for now at least, to push President Biden aside despite deep concerns about his ability to win re-election.
sentences.zh: 国会民主党高层表示，尽管对他的连任能力深感担忧，但至少目前他们不愿逼迫拜登总统退位。

sentences.en: Was there more people saying
sentences.zh: 是更多的人说

sentences.en: Biden should step down or more people saying he should step down?
sentences.zh: 拜登应该下台，还是更多的人说他应该下台？

sentences.en: We're riding with Biden.
sentences.zh: 我们全力支持拜登。

sentences.en: We're riding with Biden.
sentences.zh: 我们全力支持拜登。

sentences.en: House and Senate Democrats emerged from private meetings on Tuesday swearing allegiance to Biden.
sentences.zh: 众议院和参议院的民主党人在周二的闭门会议后露面，宣誓效忠拜登。

sentences.en: But the party remains deeply fractured.
sentences.zh: 但该党内部依然严重分裂。

sentences.en: Biden has remained strong thanks to the backing of key constituencies, including the Congressional Black Caucus, which has come out in strong support of the president's candidacy.
sentences.zh: 拜登之所以依然强势，要归功于关键选区的支持，其中包括国会黑人核心小组，该小组已经公开强烈支持总统的候选人资格。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科制作，

sentences.en: Nina Feldman, and Will Reed.
sentences.zh: 尼娜·费尔德曼和威尔·里德制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Brendan Klinkenberg with help from Paige Cowett.
sentences.zh: 由布伦丹·克林肯伯格编辑，佩奇·考维特提供协助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Dan Powell,
sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔、

sentences.en: Diane Wong, and Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 黛安·王和马里昂·洛扎诺的原创音乐，由阿丽莎·莫克斯利混音。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯贝格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 《The Daily》节目就是这样。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kittroweth.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗维斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天，

sentences.en: when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了群自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《Metro》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却最终失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: Metro。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
